system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
| ID / Issue | Seller position | Buyer should want | Recommendation / reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 General liability cap** | General warranty cap of **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | **25% / AUD 6m**. The 20% fallback requires prior written approval from Amelia Frost identifying the draft; none is given. | **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6m.** The conditional fallback is not authorised. |
| **SPA-N-002 De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 basket, with only the excess recoverable. | AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 aggregate basket, recoverable from the first dollar once exceeded. | **Reject; counter at playbook thresholds.** Seller’s thresholds are materially higher and its tipping-basket treatment is less favourable. |
| **SPA-N-003 General claims time limit** | 18 months after Completion; proposes limits apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise. | **24 months** for general claims; separate regimes preserved for other claim types. The 18-month fallback needs Amelia Frost’s written approval, which is absent. | **Reject; counter at 24 months.** Do not accept the unauthorised fallback or an across-the-board time limit. |
| **SPA-N-004 Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to general caps and time limits. | Separate regime: **100% cap, at least six years**, outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. | **Reject; insist on separate treatment.** Seller’s administrative-simplicity rationale would erode core title protections. |
| **SPA-N-005 Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims of any nature. | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. | **Reject; require the carve-out.** This is non-waivable under the playbook and must not be swallowed by general limitations. |
| **SPA-N-006 Disclosure scope** | Relies on general disclosure of the data room, public registers and records, alongside specific disclosures. | Specific fair disclosure; no deemed disclosure of the whole data room, public registers or matters discoverable through a prudent search. | **Reject the general disclosure language; retain only sufficiently specific fair disclosures.** Broad deemed disclosure could defeat warranties without identifying the relevant facts. |
| **SPA-N-007 Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by Buyer or its advisers, including matters discoverable from the data room or public records. | Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion. If any qualifier remains, limit it to named seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry; never apply it to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. | **Reject; delete the blanket bar.** It improperly treats discovery or adviser knowledge as a waiver of protection. |
| **SPA-N-008 Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. Disclosure says final consent and evidence of conditions being satisfied are not included. | Effective consent **and evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion**; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for this material customer. | **Make these conditions to Completion; do not accept consent-on-delivery.** Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue and the disclosed conditions remain unverified. |
| **SPA-N-009 Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m facility to be released after Completion. Disclosure says it remains unpaid and no final security discharge is included. | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases. Any post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost’s approval. | **Require repayment and effective releases at Completion; otherwise seek the specified approved protection.** A promised later release leaves Buyer exposed to outstanding debt/security. |
| **SPA-N-010 Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 bonuses are for Seller; not separately itemised in funds flow. On-costs are unstated. | DD-005 bonuses **plus triggered on-costs** as a specific line item or seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them. | **Require an explicit funded treatment in the funds flow.** The disclosed bonuses are conditional on Completion and are currently omitted. |
| **SPA-N-011 Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; Seller calls it adequate. DD-004 ties transfer to cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; DD-010’s AUD 180,000 is not independent bank verification. | Broaden the indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure; do not treat AUD 180,000 as independently verified either way. | **Reject the narrow limit; broaden protection and preserve cure rights.** The materials show a conditional transfer and open amount, not confirmed non-payment or confirmed payment. |
| **SPA-N-012 Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material. Disclosure does not establish access, exact scope or notification duty and states no loss amount. | Preserve logs, investigate and require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. | **Require ongoing evidence preservation, investigation and updates without asserting a confirmed breach or quantified loss.** The available record is expressly preliminary and unresolved. |
| **SPA-N-013 Sandbar renewals** | AUD 330,000 aggregate treated as ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure does not say whether renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. | Assess the three renewals; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction. | **Seek the underlying terms and assess treatment; do not automatically deduct or classify as Debt.** The disclosure leaves the relevant commercial and accounting facts open. |
| **SPA-N-014 Category separation** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims; Tax and IP are said to be settled under the general regime. | Keep Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories separate; no hidden override into the general regime. Tax/IP remain open. | **Reject the blanket override and preserve distinct regimes pending agreement.** Seller’s summary cannot settle open terms or silently subordinate other claim categories. |
| **SPA-N-015 Title verification** | Relies on DD-012 share register showing Seller as holder of 100%; no Buyer verification is stated. | Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority; DD-012 is an internal supplied source, not independent proof. | **Require independent verification.** A register identifying the recorded holder alone does not establish the full title position or authority. |
| **SPA-N-016 Tax/IP open terms** | Seller considers Tax and IP positions settled under the general regime. | Tax/IP terms remain **open**; do not assume unlimited liability or a resolution. | **Treat as unresolved and negotiate separately.** Seller’s assertion is not buyer approval or evidence of agreement. |
=== END ADVICE ===
